name: Dhu al-Qa'dah
intro:
The month of Dhu al-Qa'dah is, on the one hand, a reminder of days of joy through several births, and on the other hand, a reminder of days of sorrow through several martyrdoms and other incidents. The days 1, 9, 11, 23, 25, 26 and 30 contain the important days of this month.
The birth of Imam Reza (PBUH) and the birth of Hazrat Ma'sumah (PBUH) are the joyous news of this month, and this joy is doubled by the death of Ash'ath ibn Qays.
The martyrdom of Imam Reza and Imam Jawad (PBUT) are the days of sorrow of this month.
The Battle of Badr al-Sughra, the Battle of Banu Qurayzah, the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, and the Prophet's (SAWW) departure for the Farewell Pilgrimage are important pages of Islamic history.

events.title: Birth of Hazrat Ma'sumah (PBUH)
events.text:
On this day in the year 173 AH, the noble daughter of Musa ibn Ja'far (PBUH), Hazrat Fatimah Ma'sumah (PBUH), was born.
Her honorable father was Imam Musa ibn Ja'far (PBUH), and her venerable mother was Lady Najmah (PBUH), the mother of Imam Reza (PBUH). Her blessed name was Fatimah, her title was Ma'sumah, and in the household of the Seventh Imam (PBUH), Hazrat Ma'sumah (PBUH) was called “Fatimah the Greater.”
sources: Tabaqat Ibn Sa'd: vol. 2, p. 51. The Life of Hazrat Ma'sumah (PBUH) and the History of Qom: p. 34. Fatimah bint al-Imam Musa al-Kazim (PBUH): p. 14.
Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 48, pp. 288, 303.

events.title: Battle of Badr al-Sughra
events.text: On this day in the year 4 AH, the Battle of Badr al-Sughra took place; it is also called “Badr al-Maw'id” and “Badr al-Thalithah.”
sources: Nasikh al-Tawarikh: Hijrah volume, p. 197. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 20, p. 182.

events.title: Death of Ash'ath ibn Qays
events.text:
On the first night of Dhu al-Qa'dah in the year 40 AH, Ash'ath ibn Qays al-Kindi rushed to the depths of Hell.
Imam Sadiq (PBUH) said: “Ash'ath ibn Qays was a partner in the murder of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), his daughter Ju'dah poisoned Imam Mujtaba (PBUH), and his son Muhammad was a partner in the murder of Imam Husayn (PBUH).”
Ash'ath embraced Islam in the tenth year of the Hijrah along with a group from his tribe, and after the Prophet (SAWW) he apostatized. Abu Bakr arrested him and gave him his own sister in marriage on the condition that he be her husband. From this marriage Ju'dah and Muhammad were born; Ju'dah became the murderer of Imam Hasan (PBUH), and Muhammad joined the army of Umar ibn Sa'd at Karbala and also played a significant role in the arrest of Muslim ibn Aqil (PBUH).
On the day of Ashura, because of an insolence he showed toward Imam Husayn (PBUH), when he had stepped aside to relieve himself, a scorpion stung him, and with his private parts exposed he entered the fire of Hell.
sources: Mustadrakat Ilm al-Rijal al-Hadith: vol. 1, p. 688.
Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 42, p. 228.
Riyahin al-Shari'ah: vol. 3, p. 59. Mustadrakat Ilm al-Rijal al-Hadith: vol. 1, p. 688.
Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 44, p. 317.

events.title: Hazrat Muslim's Letter to Imam Husayn (PBUH)
events.text: On this day in the year 60 AH, 27 days before his martyrdom, Hazrat Muslim (PBUH) wrote a letter to Imam Husayn (PBUH) and informed him that 18,000 people had pledged allegiance to him.
sources: Nafas al-Mahmum: p. 84. Waqa'i al-Shuhur: p. 213.

events.title: Birth of Imam Reza (PBUH)
events.text:
On a Thursday in the year 148 AH, Imam Reza (PBUH) was born in Medina the Radiant. 11 Dhu al-Hijjah and 11 Rabi' al-Awwal have also been mentioned as the date of his birth.
His father was Musa ibn Ja'far (PBUH), and his mother was Umm al-Banin Najmah (PBUH). His blessed name was Ali, his kunyah was Abu al-Hasan, and his special kunyah was Abu Ali.
The titles of the Imam were Siraj Allah, Nur al-Huda, Qurrat Ayn al-Mu'minin, Makidat al-Mulhidin, Kufw al-Malik, Kafi al-Khalq, Rabb al-Sarir, Ri'ab al-Tadbir (meaning “the reformer”), Fadil, Sabir, Wafi, Siddiq, and Radi.
When he was born, his father, Hazrat Musa ibn Ja'far (PBUH), ordered that their son be brought to him.
The Imam was wrapped in a white cloth and taken into the presence of his father. His father recited the adhan in the right ear and the iqamah in the left ear of Hazrat Reza (PBUH), placed water of the Euphrates in his blessed mouth, and then returned him to his venerable mother, Najmah (PBUH).
sources: I'lam al-Wara: vol. 2, p. 40. Jala' al-'Uyun: p. 544. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 90. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 49, p. 10.
Fayd al-'Allam: p. 119. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 49, p. 304.
I'lam al-Wara: vol. 2, p. 40. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 49, p. 10. Irshad: vol. 2, p. 246.
Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 49, p. 10.
Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 49, p. 10.
Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 49, p. 9.

events.title: Martyrdom of Imam Reza (PBUH)
events.text: According to one account, on this day in the year 203 AH, Hazrat Reza (PBUH) was martyred.
sources: Masar al-Shi'ah: p. 16. al-'Udad al-Qawiyyah: p. 275. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 97.

events.title: Battle of Banu Qurayzah
events.text: On this day in the year 4 AH, the Expedition of Banu Qurayzah took place. The Muslims numbered 3,000, and one man named Khallad ibn Suwayd was martyred. The disbelievers numbered 900, all of whom were killed. According to one account, this battle took place in Shawwal.
sources: al-Mawsu'ah al-Kubra fi Ghazawat al-Nabi al-A'zam (SAWW): vol. 3, p. 192.
Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 19, p. 170.

events.title: Imam Reza's (PBUH) Departure from Medina Toward Merv
events.text: On this day in the year 200 AH, Hazrat Reza (PBUH) set out from Medina toward Merv.
sources: Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 8, p. 556.

events.title: The Prophet's (SAWW) Departure from Medina for the Farewell Pilgrimage
events.text: On this day in the year 10 AH, the Prophet (SAWW) set out with his companions from Medina for the Farewell Pilgrimage and Ghadir. Some accounts have reported the 23rd and others the 25th of Dhu al-Qa'dah.
sources: al-Kafi: vol. 4, p. 248.
al-Ghadir: vol. 1, p. 9. Qala'id al-Nuhur: Shawwal vol., p. 272.

events.title: Martyrdom of Imam Jawad (PBUH)
events.text:
On this day in the year 220 AH, Imam Jawad (PBUH) was martyred by the poison of al-Mu'tasim, and at the time of his martyrdom, 25 years, three months and 12 days had passed of his blessed age. Regarding the date of his martyrdom, 5 Dhu al-Qa'dah, 5 Dhu al-Hijjah of the year 219 AH, 6 Dhu al-Hijjah and 25 Dhu al-Hijjah have also been mentioned.
After the martyrdom of Hazrat Reza (PBUH), al-Ma'mun summoned Jawad al-A'immah (PBUH) to Baghdad and married his daughter Umm al-Fadl to him. After a time, as the Imam (PBUH) was very distressed by al-Ma'mun's mistreatment, he went to Mecca for the Hajj. He then went to Medina and remained there until al-Ma'mun went to his doom and his brother al-Mu'tasim became caliph.
Al-Mu'tasim harbored a particular envy toward the Imam, and summoned that infallible Imam (PBUH) together with Umm al-Fadl to Baghdad. In the presence of the elders of the Shia and the trustworthy among his companions in Medina, the Imam introduced Imam Hadi (PBUH) as the Imam after him and handed over to him the trusts of the Imamate, and on 28 Muharram of the year 220 AH he entered Baghdad. Umm al-Fadl, at the instigation of her uncle al-Mu'tasim, and according to one account Ja'far ibn al-Ma'mun, poisoned the Imam (PBUH) at the age of 25.
sources: Irshad: vol. 2, p. 295. I'lam al-Wara: vol. 2, p. 106. Tawdih al-Maqasid: p. 29. Kashf al-Ghummah: vol. 2, p. 370. Usul al-Kafi: vol. 2, p. 541. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 103. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 50, pp. 8, 10. Qala'id al-Nuhur: Dhu al-Qa'dah vol., p. 279.
Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 50, pp. 11, 12, 14, 15, 17.
Tatimmat al-Muntaha: p. 300.
Sharh Ihqaq al-Haqq: vol. 12, pp. 414, 416.
A summary from Qala'id al-Nuhur: Dhu al-Qa'dah vol., p. 279.

events.title: Treaty of Hudaybiyyah
events.text:
In the sixth year of the Hijrah, in the month of Dhu al-Qa'dah, the Prophet (SAWW) set out for Mecca to perform the Umrah rites. The number of Muslims accompanying him was 1,220 or 400, and they took 70 camels with them for sacrifice.
They entered the state of ihram at Masjid al-Shajarah, and a day's journey from Mecca, at a place called Hudaybiyyah, they halted by a well. The water of the well ran out within a short time, and when the Prophet was informed, by the miracle of prophethood the water of the well increased so much that it gushed like a spring.
The disbelievers, having learned of the march, prevented the Prophet from entering Mecca. The Prophet took another pledge of allegiance from his companions, called the “Pledge of Ridwan.” It was agreed that the Prophet would perform the Hajj and Umrah the following year as a make-up, and a treaty was concluded between the Muslims and the disbelievers, under which, subject to certain conditions, there would be no war between them for ten years. A group of the companions were disheartened by this treaty, and Umar ibn al-Khattab said: “I never doubted the prophethood of Muhammad as I did on the day of Hudaybiyyah,” and he kept saying to the Prophet (SAWW): How can we submit to this humiliation and accept this settlement!!
The Prophet said: I am the Messenger of God, and I do nothing except by God's command. Umar said: You told us we were going to visit the Kaaba and perform Umrah, so what happened? The Prophet (SAWW) said: Did I say this would be done this year? Umar said: No! He said: Then why do you dispute?!!
On the return from Hudaybiyyah, Surah al-Fath was revealed to the Prophet.
sources: al-Isti'ab: vol. 4, p. 1917.
al-Ta'ajjub (Karajaki): p. 59.
Muntaha al-Amal: vol. 1, p. 76. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 20, pp. 317, 316, 335; vol. 18, p. 37; vol. 86, p. 111.

honorifics.(SAWW): Sallallahu Alayhi wa Alihi wa Sallam — peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his progeny (the Prophet Muhammad)
honorifics.(PBUH): Peace Be Upon Him (used for Imams, Prophets and other holy figures, male)
honorifics.(SA): Salamullah Alayha — peace be upon her (Lady Fatima, Lady Umm Kulthum, Lady Zaynab, Lady Narjis, etc.)
honorifics.(PBUT): Peace Be Upon Them (plural, e.g. the Ahl al-Bayt / the Infallible Imams)
honorifics.(ATFS): Ajjalallahu Ta'ala Farajahu ash-Sharif — may Allah hasten his noble reappearance (the Imam of the Age)
honorifics.(RA): Rahimahullah — may Allah have mercy on him
